diagram_classification: computistical / natural-philosophical (cycle of the year and seasons, possibly linked to the four elements)
interpretation: A large circle, probably standing for the year or the cosmos, contains four sets of coloured arcs (red, grey-blue, yellow, dark brown). The arcs cross and overlap one another, and each seems to be anchored on the circumference. The most likely reading is that each colour is one of four recurring temporal or natural principles, probably the four seasons, perhaps with their associated elements or qualities. The overlaps would show that the seasons succeed and merge into one another in a continuous cycle rather than being sharply separated. The marginal rubric appears to read 'hiemps temporalis' ('seasonal winter'), and the nearby text seems to contain 'intellegitur' ('is understood'), which would fit a gloss on time or the seasons. The exact assignment of colours to seasons or elements cannot be established from the image.
evidence: Visible: a circle with a double orange-red outline; four sets of arcs in different colours that cut across each other and the circle; a text block around the figure; a partly legible rubric at the lower left ('hiemps temporalis') and a few words at the lower right ('intellegitur tribu...'). External: early medieval computistical and natural-science manuscripts (Isidorian or Bedan traditions) often use circular or interlaced figures for the year, the seasons, and the elements and their qualities. No specific source is claimed. The lack of labels on the arcs prevents a firm identification of the colours, and the reading of the legible words is tentative, so certainty is low.
